es_0aTIt4BztQW9G4hW.q:
In a web server, ten WebPages are stored with the URLs of the form
http://www.yourname.com/\(var\).html; where, \(var\) is a different number from \(1\) to \(10\) for each Webpage. Suppose, the client stores the Webpage with \(var=1\) (say \(W1\)) in local machine, edits and then tests. Rest of the WebPages remains on the web server. \(W1\) contains several relative URLs of the form “\(var\).html” referring to the other WebPages. Which one of the following statements needs to be added in \(W1,\) so that all the relative URLs in \(W1\) refer to the appropriate WebPages on the web server?
es_0aTIt4BztQW9G4hW.e:
**Key idea:** the HTML `<base>` element (placed in `<head>`) sets the base URL against which **all** relative URLs in the document are resolved.

$W1$ is now opened from the local machine, so a relative link such as `3.html` would otherwise resolve to a local file. Adding

```html
<base href="http://www.yourname.com/">
```

makes every relative URL `var.html` in $W1$ resolve to `http://www.yourname.com/var.html` on the web server, which is exactly what is needed.

Why the others fail:
- (A), (C): `<a href=...>` creates a single hyperlink. It does not change how the other relative URLs in the page are resolved.
- (D): `<base>` has no `range` attribute. One base URL already covers all relative links.

**Answer: (B)**

es_OpyiMztQtO9YlejI.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about \(HTTP\) cookies?
o: A cookie is a piece of code that has the potential to compromise the security of an Internet user
A cookie gains entry to the user’s work area through an \(HTTP\) header
A cookie has an expiry date and time
Cookies can be used to track the browsing pattern of a user at a particular site
es_OpyiMztQtO9YlejI.e:
**Key idea:** an HTTP cookie is a small piece of **data** (a name–value pair plus attributes), not executable code.

- **(A) Not correct.** A cookie is plain text stored by the browser and sent back to the server. It cannot execute, so it is not "a piece of code". The real concern with cookies is privacy (tracking), not code that attacks the machine.
- **(B) Correct.** The server sets a cookie through the `Set-Cookie` HTTP response header, and the browser returns it in the `Cookie` request header.
- **(C) Correct.** Persistent cookies carry an `Expires`/`Max-Age` attribute. Session cookies expire when the browser closes.
- **(D) Correct.** Because the cookie identifies the browser on every request, a site can link the pages a user visits and track their browsing pattern. Third-party cookies extend this across sites.

**Answer: (A)**
